shape.description: Same body, legs, arches, rails and two opposite tabs as B-01, with a round hole through the cup floor at its centre, marble-sized or bigger. Stacked on a block, it looks into that block's cup.

physics.behaviour: Drops the marble down inside the stack; it does not carry it across. It falls one slot per hole block to the next solid cup, usually a B-02 whose mouth leads to the exit track. Chained hole blocks make a chimney.

evidence.shows: white B-04 on B-02 and on B-01, over T-02 ends; hole visible in cup floor
real white block in a stack: rails, tab, arch
round side hole sits exactly at a joint: arch of upper block over cup end of lower block; red T-08 plugs in there

assumptions: Axes: +x = E, +y = S, z up; z is in slots above this block's own feet. Marble seat in a cup is z=0.68.

Joint rule: a block body is about a cube; pitch is 1 slot; rails stand 0.17 slot higher and nest inside the block above. Each face has a low arch, as tall as the cup is deep (0.33 slot). So the arch of an upper block plus the cup end of the lower block make a round hole at the joint, about 0.65 slot across. The cup-end port and the side round hole are the SAME port: it is a notch when the stack ends there and a hole when a block sits on top. Height is the same either way, n-0.32 slots for the nth block.
The owner states the round hole goes through the cup. Falling through is inferred from that plus the plan stacks; no plan page labels it.
Marble dropping into a B-01 below: seats and rolls out either cup end, direction uncertain.
Extreme plans print this white block as B-03 (extracted_extreme.json); Launchpad prints B-04. Treated as the same shape as B-03 by drawing, colour differs.
